item.title: Wake-induced dynamics of soft-impact oscillators: Analysis and electronic experimental validation
item.description: arXiv:2610.14718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article presents an electronic experimental validation of discontinuity-induced bifurcations, including period-adding cascades, in a wake-induced dynamical system subjected to soft impacts. A cylindrical structure immersed in a cross-flow undergoes vortex-induced vibrations and interacts with a movable barrier during the upper and lower branches of the response. The structural motion is modelled as a harmonic oscillator, while the fluctuating lift is represented by a Van der Pol oscillator. The soft contact interaction between the structure and the movable barrier is modelled using a bilinear restoring force, resulting in a piecewise-smooth wake-oscillator system. A systematic numerical investigation reveals period-adding cascades of periodic orbits interspersed with chaotic responses as the barrier distance and fluid-flow velocity are varied. The results are experimentally validated using an inductorless electronic analogue of the piecewise-smooth wake model constructed from operational amplifiers and implemented on a printed-circuit board to improve experimental robustness. The route to instability of the periodic and aperiodic responses is further characterized using Floquet multipliers and Lyapunov exponents. A zero-time transverse discontinuity mapping is implemented to account for the evolution of perturbations in the local neighborhood of the discontinuity boundary during stability analysis. The combined numerical, experimental, and stability analyses demonstrate the role of soft impacts in generating complex nonlinear responses in the wake-induced system.
item.dc:creator: Rohit Chawla, Soumyajit Seth, Vikram Pakrashi

item.title: Nonlinear Signal Transmission and Harmonic Generation in Plasma Oscillator Chain with Coupling Asymmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.14722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate signal transmission in a one-dimensional chain of $n$ locally coupled plasma oscillators with asymmetric bidirectional coupling $(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$. Our results reveal a clear contrast between symmetric and asymmetric interactions: while symmetric coupling suppresses signal propagation, coupling asymmetry enables efficient nonlinear transmission across the network. In particular, sustained long range transmission is achieved when the forward coupling strength exceeds the backward coupling strength ($\epsilon_1 > \epsilon_2$), as demonstrated through a comprehensive phase diagram in the $(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2)$ parameter space. Furthermore, under asymmetric diffusive coupling, signal transmission can persist even when the first few oscillators in the chain undergo oscillation death. A central finding of this study is the intrinsic generation of higher harmonics induced by nonlinear interactions, leading to a pronounced reversal of vibrational resonance. This nonlinear redistribution of energy facilitates selective amplification and robust propagation of specific frequency components.
item.dc:creator: K. Abirami, Miguel A. Prado-Reynoso, Miguel A. F. Sanju\'an

item.title: Energy Transmission and Harmonic Propagation in Unidirectionally Coupled Plasma Oscillator Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.14752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate signal transmission in a network of unidirectionally coupled plasma oscillators, where only the first oscillator is driven by a weak periodic input. As the signal propagates through the network, nonlinear interactions generate higher-order harmonic components. Spectral analysis identifies five distinct transmission patterns for the fundamental frequency and odd harmonics, and four patterns for even harmonics, encompassing damped propagation, undamped transmission, and localized amplification. The transmission characteristics are governed by both the coupling strength and system parameters. Furthermore, we analyze how variations in these key parameters shape the overall signal dynamics.
item.dc:creator: K. Abirami, Miguel A. Prado-Reynoso, Miguel A. F. Sanju\'an

item.title: Inferred and Residual Parameter Interactions in Syntax Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.15598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What makes natural languages diversify, in their syntactic structure, even when sharing a largely common origin? We refine our simple model, which focuses on the glassy dynamics induced by a network of interactions between syntactic parameters. Distinguishing between symmetric interaction weights that can be inferred from the observed statistics of syntax across many languages, and additional asymmetric weights assigned at random, we show that both components are needed, with similar overall strength, to account for plausible long-term syntactic dynamics. An approximate balance can combine the glassy metastability provided by the inferred weights with the chaotic diversification induced by the residual asymmetric weights.
item.dc:creator: Hediye Yarahmadi, Alessandro Treves

item.title: Geometric Transition of Latent Dynamics in Intermittent Chaos: SVD-based Effective Dimension for Detection and Proactive Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.16495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the geometric detection of latent dynamic transitions (where the latent space is defined as a finite-dimensional state space reconstructed via a delay-embedding Hankel matrix) in mutually coupled phase-locked loops (PLLs) exhibiting on-off intermittent chaos. We propose a data-driven approach to identify the transition of the effective dimension in latent dynamics as a precursor to physical bursting events. By applying Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) to a Hankel matrix constructed from high-resolution oversampled data, we extract the effective dimension that reflects the dynamical shift of intrinsic variables - from a synchronized two-dimensional manifold to a higher-dimensional chaotic state - prior to the actual burst. This geometric indicator enables a proactive, event-driven intervention using Pyragas-type delayed feedback control, which is activated only when the detected dimension exceeds a critical threshold. Simulation results demonstrate that this geometric precursor effectively compensates for control latencies and substantially reduces accumulated control energy compared to conventional continuous feedback. The findings establish a methodological strategy for stabilizing infinite-dimensional delayed systems by exploiting early warning signals embedded in dimensional transitions of latent dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Takashi Hikihara, Tetsushi Saburi

item.title: Information transfer as a new indicator of approaching local bifurcations: saddle-node, pitchfork and Hopf bifurcations
item.description: arXiv:2610.17529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Early warning signals are key tools for anticipating qualitative changes in the dynamics of complex systems. In this work, we investigate whether an information-theoretic measure designed to characterize directional causal dependencies between observables can provide early warning of the approach to bifurcations. The measure considered is the rate of information transfer, which has been successfully applied to characterize directional dependencies in a broad range of fields, from economics to climate science. Three fundamental local bifurcations are considered: saddle-node, pitchfork, and Hopf bifurcations. We first investigate idealized (quasi-)potential stochastic systems for which analytical expressions for the rate of information transfer can be derived. Distinct signatures are found for the three bifurcation types. In particular, the rate of information transfer displays a strong increase and divergence when approaching the saddle-node bifurcation, whereas smoother but systematic changes are found near the pitchfork and Hopf bifurcations. The approach is then tested using low-order climate models exhibiting the same types of bifurcations. The results confirm that changes in the rate of information transfer can precede the corresponding dynamical transitions, suggesting that directional information transfer provides a useful complementary early-warning indicator for detecting the approach to critical transitions in nonlinear stochastic systems.
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane Vannitsem, Carlos A. Pires, X. San Liang

item.title: Beyond RMSE and Granger Gain: Multi-Horizon Forecast-Error Entropy for Nonlinear Predictive Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.18390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate whether the past of an auxiliary time series provides predictive information about a target beyond that contained in the target's own history. We compare matched out-of-sample target-only and target-plus-source forecasts and introduce the forecast-error distribution entropy (FEDE) predictive-causality framework, where predictive causality is understood in the Granger sense: auxiliary history is informative when it improves prediction beyond the target's own past. FEDE quantifies how the full signed forecast-error distribution changes across prediction horizons. Controlled nonlinear benchmarks hide source-target dependence behind nonlinear transformations not supplied to the predictors. LightGBM recovers these hidden channels, whereas Ridge does not. Across four equal-power nonlinearities and four noise levels, the mean response-sensitivity statistic for FEDE remains 29.00, 27.47, 23.22, and 28.67, compared with 14.09, 10.68, 12.67, and 12.71 for mean log-RMSE gain. Directional and source controls separate the true source-to-target channel from the reverse direction and from independent periodic, quasiperiodic, chaotic, and autoregressive auxiliaries. Chronological Granger-style comparisons show strong model-form dependence: a degree-2 polynomial model is exceptionally sensitive to the matched quadratic channel but becomes weak or oppositely aligned for other nonlinearities, while basic convergent cross mapping is weak or directionally inconsistent in this stochastic, partly non-invertible setting. FEDE remains positively aligned across all 108 tested combinations of window length, history length, and maximum forecast horizon. Together, these results establish FEDE as a sensitive and robust horizon-resolved tool that extracts predictive information beyond conventional error-magnitude measures when the nonlinear interaction form is unknown. Code available in Zenodo.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Velichko

item.title: Random wave chaos on momentum-fractionated microstate geometries
item.description: arXiv:2610.15918v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of D1-D5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. We probe the chaos through the dynamics of null geodesics and waves. On fractionated backgrounds, both geodesics and waves show uniformly strong chaos (large chaotic sea and near-perfect agreement with the Berry random wave hypothesis). In contrast, geodesics and waves on single-mode (non-fractionated) superstrata are closer to separability (although still chaotic). We discuss a possibility that such dichotomy can be related to the expectation that monotone BPS states are less chaotic than fortuitous ones. Finally, we explain why our chaos probes are meaningful for microstate geometries even though they become trivial in the black hole limit.
item.dc:creator: Vladan Djuki\'c, Mihailo \v{C}ubrovi\'c

item.title: Universal Boolean Computation in Negatively Coupled Circle Map Lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.16290v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the computational capabilities of a one-dimensional lattice of negatively coupled circle maps in its traveling wave regime. We interpret propagating waves as information carriers and exploit their interactions to implement Boolean logic. The logical states are encoded by the propagation direction of the traveling waves, while the presence or absence of a wave at a designated output location represents the logical output. Using controlled wave collisions, we demonstrate the realization of NAND and NOR gates along with other basic gates. Since NAND and NOR operations are functionally complete, the results establish that the traveling wave regime of the negatively coupled circle-map lattice supports universal Boolean computation in principle. The demonstrated logical operations remain valid over a finite range of the coupling strength \epsilon and map parameter \omega, indicating robustness of the computational scheme to parameter variations. Our results therefore demonstrate that computational functionality can emerge from the collective nonlinear dynamics of a coupled map lattice, providing a con- nection between the dynamical properties of traveling wave states and collision based information processing.
item.dc:creator: Priyanka D. Bhoyar, Prashant M. Gade

item.title: Multivariate phase-space interpretation of ensemble forecasts: A comparison of physical and AI models
item.description: arXiv:2610.16422v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ensemble forecasts from the ECMWF's Integrated Forecasting System (IFS) and the Artificial Intelligence Forecasting System (AIFS-ENS) are compared using a multi-dimensional evaluation framework. Within this framework, the uncertainty is interpreted as the linear subspace spanned by the ensemble members in phase space, from which various geometric properties are extracted. As revealed by the analysis, the error does not entirely lie in this subspace, but is reasonably well calibrated in all directions. Moreover, the framework allows to quantify that this subspace critically depends on the number of ensemble members, suggesting that the current setups only partially represent the uncertainty subspace. This phase-space interpretation furthermore allows a direct comparison of the error-representation patterns of AIFS-ENS and IFS by computing the principal angles between the subspaces: IFS and AIFS ensemble subspaces do not entirely overlap in phase space, even though they were shown to have similar abilities to represent the amplitude and the structure of the error.
item.dc:creator: Martin Bonte, St\'ephane Vannitsem

item.title: Reverse quantum aging: Restoring rhythmicity from quantum aging state
item.description: arXiv:2610.16638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum aging transition has recently been reported, whereby the oscillatory dynamics of a network of globally coupled quantum self-sustained oscillators is degraded sharply when the fraction of inactive nodes exceeds a critical value. Here we explore the reverse process: the revival of rhythmic dynamics from an aged state in a quantum oscillator network by introducing a controlled incoherent single-boson pumping channel. Using a self-consistent quantum master equation in the Lindblad form for globally coupled active--inactive quantum Stuart--Landau oscillators, we show that increasing the pumping strength progressively suppresses the aging transition and eventually eliminates it, restoring rhythmicity even when all oscillators are inactive. Remarkably, complete compensation of the coupling-induced dissipative loss is not required; a substantially weaker pumping strength is sufficient to eliminate the aging transition. We show that the revival is governed by a redistribution of the Fock-state population of the inactive oscillators toward higher-occupation states. Our results establish controlled incoherent pumping as an effective mechanism for restoring dynamical robustness in quantum oscillator networks.
item.dc:creator: Bulti Paul, Biswabibek Bandyopadhyay, Tanmoy Banerjee

item.title: Limit cycles govern wave energy accumulation in space-time-varying materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.16847v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the amplification and concentration of wave energy in smooth, periodic space-time media through the dynamics of the characteristic curves of the associated wave equation. In an impedance-matched setting, we show that stable limit cycles attract neighbouring characteristics, focusing the wave energy density. The exponential attraction rate is estimated analytically from the system's Lyapunov exponent. We further show that the attraction of characteristics and energy accumulation persist under a range of nonperiodic perturbations. Finally, we present a Floquet-Fourier numerical method for computing stable and unstable limit cycles and their attraction rates. Throughout, we exemplify the results using the example of modulation given by a superposition of travelling waves, revealing saddle--node bifurcations where limit cycles may appear depending on the relative wave speeds. Full-wave simulations confirm that the characteristic mechanism continues to describe energy accumulation beyond the impedance-matched case.
item.dc:creator: Bryn Davies, Erik Orvehed Hiltunen

item.title: Bifurcation Structure of Double Hysteresis and Isolated Branches in a Parametric Duffing Nanoresonator
item.description: arXiv:2610.17052v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Direct and parametric driving together generate nonlinear response structures beyond conventional Duffing hysteresis, including multiple switching regions and isolated branches. Understanding how these structures are connected requires identifying the bifurcations that reorganize the response as the parametric excitation is varied. At a phase difference of 45 degrees between the direct and parametric excitations, we experimentally and analytically determine how the steady-state response changes as the parametric excitation is increased. A single resonance peak first splits into two while the response remains single valued. Two successive cusp bifurcations then create two saddle-node pairs and establish a double-hysteretic response. At the parametric-instability threshold, one saddle node of each pair is displaced towards unbounded amplitude and detuning, and an isolated-branch structure emerges above threshold. A parametric representation of the steady state distinguishes amplitude extrema from genuine saddle-node bifurcations and provides analytical conditions for these changes. Measurements on a dielectrically actuated pre-stressed SiN nanostring reproduce the predicted response and associated switching behavior. These results establish the bifurcation pathway connecting the different response structures at this phase configuration, providing a systematic basis for controlling multistability and switching in parametrically driven nonlinear resonators.
item.dc:creator: Dingda Zhang, Maria Kallergi, Chanyoung So, Eva M. Weig, Ahmed A. Barakat

item.title: Cyclotomic Structure and Exact Recurrences in Floquet Many-Body Quantum Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.17137v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Periodically driven quantum systems exhibit a wide range of complex dynamics, including chaos. Yet, at special parameter values, their evolution can recur exactly. Several quantum protocols have recently been proposed that exploit exact Floquet recurrences to demonstrate genuine quantum advantage. Such recurrences can be studied through the arithmetic structure of the Floquet unitary. In this work, we establish a necessary and sufficient arithmetic criterion for exact recurrence and determine the minimal recurrence period when one exists. Because recurrence is a global property of the unitary, it holds for every initial state. Applying our framework requires only knowledge of the number field associated with the Hamiltonian parameters. We demonstrate the method using the kicked Ising chain, establishing exact recurrences in both Clifford and non-Clifford regimes. We further show that, in the recurrent non-Clifford regime, magic--a resource for quantum computation--is generated at intermediate times and undergoes exact periodic revivals enforced by the recurrence of the full Floquet unitary. By connecting number theory, quantum many-body dynamics, and quantum information, our work shows that exact recurrence extends beyond Clifford circuits and opens new avenues for magic generation and quantum hardware benchmarking.
item.dc:creator: Amit Anand, Dinesh Valluri, Shohini Ghose

item.title: Controlling synchronization dynamics via physics-informed neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2601.00178v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Synchronization control in networked dynamical systems requires regulating not only whether coherence is achieved, but also when and to what extent it emerges. We propose a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for continuous-time synchronization regulation, in which system trajectories and control inputs are jointly parameterized and constrained by the governing dynamics. Macroscopic synchronization objectives are imposed directly at the trajectory level by enforcing persistence conditions on the order parameter after a prescribed target time. This formulation enables simultaneous control of synchronization time and coherence level without assuming any explicit feedback law or solving a strict optimal control problem. Numerical studies on networked Kuramoto oscillators demonstrate smooth synchronization with reduced transient control effort and competitive cumulative cost relative to analytical baselines. The framework remains effective in non-gradient and frustrated dynamics, highlighting physics-informed neural control as a flexible trajectory-level approach to synchronization regulation.
item.dc:creator: Kaiming Luo

item.title: Chimera States in Wheel Networks
item.description: arXiv:2601.01411v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chimera states, characterized by the coexistence of coherent and incoherent dynamics, are a hallmark of symmetry-breaking phenomena in networks of coupled oscillators. Here, we investigate the role of higher-order interactions in the emergence of chimera states in wheel networks of R\"ossler and Lorenz oscillators with pairwise and higher-order interactions under diffusive, conjugate, and mean-field diffusive coupling. Using multiple random initial conditions, we quantify the prevalence of synchronized, desynchronized, chimera, and synchronized cluster states. Chimera states emerge across all three coupling mechanisms as symmetry-broken states among the structurally and dynamically equivalent peripheral oscillators. Higher-order interactions substantially reorganize the dynamical landscape; in particular, they shift chimera states toward weaker pairwise coupling under diffusive coupling, predominantly support them at moderate coupling strengths under conjugate coupling, and yield comparatively less prevalent chimera states under mean-field diffusive coupling. These effects depend strongly on the intrinsic oscillator dynamics, particularly at larger higher-order coupling strengths. Overall, higher-order interactions neither universally promote nor suppress chimera states; rather, their influence is governed by the interplay between network symmetry, coupling mechanism, and intrinsic oscillator dynamics. The observed collective states are quantitatively characterized using two proposed statistical measures, while master-stability-function analysis provides a stability-based explanation for the loss of complete synchronization and the emergence of nonsynchronous dynamical regimes.
item.dc:creator: Medha Bhindwar, Ashwathi Poolamanna, Yuvrajsingh Pravinsingh Patil, Chandrakala Meena

item.title: Causal analysis of inner and outer motions in near-wall turbulence
item.description: arXiv:2404.08907v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we study the causality of near-wall inner and outer turbulent motions. The inner motions are defined as the self-sustained near-wall cycle, and the outer motions as those living in the logarithmic layer exhibiting footprints on the near-wall region. Causal inference with three typical methods is performed, \emph{i.e.} transfer entropy, information flow, and SURD (synergistic--unique--redundant decomposition of causality). The causal inference methods are first applied to several canonical problems to illustrate their abilities, including a linear problem, a non-linear problem, and a low-dimensional model of near-wall turbulence. It is demonstrated that all three methods can produce consistent causal findings. Furthermore, we study the causalities between the inner and outer turbulent motions in a channel flow using the three methods with an improved inner-outer decomposition method. It is revealed that both the inner and outer motions are causally self-sustained, supporting the self-sustaining mechanism of turbulent motions at all scales. We also find that there are top-down and bottom-up causalities between the outer motions and their near-wall footprints owing to the dynamical coherence of inclined large-scale turbulent motions. More interestingly, pressure is identified to play an active role in the inner-outer causalities and may act as a bridge in linking the inner and outer turbulent motions.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Fluid Mechanics, 2026, vol. 1043, A18
item.dc:creator: Jingxuan Zhang, Zhengping Zhu, Limin Wang, Wei Gao, Ruifeng Hu

item.title: Chaotic Billiard Lasers
item.description: arXiv:2604.23614v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This chapter provides an overview of chaotic billiard lasers as a prominent branch of quantum chaos. These lasers offer an ideal experimental platform for demonstrating the principles of quantum chaos within a physical system. We begin by introducing the fundamental principles of chaotic ray dynamics in optical microcavities, where the transition from regular to fully chaotic dynamics fundamentally alters the underlying wavefunctions and lasing properties. A central focus is placed on "chaos-assisted light emission," which serves as a practical manifestation of "chaos-assisted tunneling" -- a hallmark phenomenon in the study of quantum chaos. We discuss both theoretical frameworks and experimental validations, demonstrating how chaotic orbits facilitate the coupling between evanescently localized modes and far-field emission. Furthermore, exploring how the presence of a gain medium influences established results from quantum chaos research remains a fundamental and intriguing problem in physics. To address this, we establish a rigorous and comprehensive derivation of the Maxwell-Bloch equations for two-dimensional microcavity lasers, specifically examining their application to fully chaotic, stadium-shaped billiard lasers. By bridging the gap between nonlinear lasing processes and chaotic wavefunctions, this chapter highlights the unique potential of chaotic billiards for controlling light-matter interactions and shaping the next generation of unconventional coherent light sources.
item.dc:creator: Takahisa Harayama

item.title: High-throughput full-f gyrokinetics of the tokamak boundary
item.description: arXiv:2605.01117v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Full-f gyrokinetics of the tokamak boundary have so far been limited to individual, expert-curated cases. We report hundreds of concurrent and unsupervised simulations of the edge and scrape-off layer (SOL) in a geometry based on the Tokamak \`a Configuration Variable (TCV), scanning triangularity, elongation and heating power, each evolving turbulence for more than a millisecond, i.e. about two energy confinement times. Without tuned transport coefficients or experimental inputs, the ensemble reproduces the range of SOL heat-flux decay lengths measured in TCV, as well as the reduced SOL density fluctuations and the improved confinement of negative triangularity. The effect of triangularity on confinement is power dependent. At high power, negative triangularity improves the ion energy confinement by weakening the dominant microinstability rather than by a stronger sheared flow. At low power, positive triangularity flattens the ion temperature profile across the separatrix, which we attribute to a longer distance between the trapped ions and the cold recycling source. Local linear gyrokinetic calculations and the transport coefficients extracted from the turbulent fluxes consistently indicate a trapped-electron-mode regime, in which the conductive heat flux at the separatrix is carried by the electrons and the ion energy transport is convective. This article details the simulation setup, the ensemble statistics and the verification of the results, which are also summarized in a companion Letter.
item.dc:creator: A. C. D. Hoffmann, M. Francisquez, T. N. Bernard, G. W. Hammett

item.title: Photonic reservoir computing with complex networks
item.description: arXiv:2607.23285v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Photonic reservoir computing has attracted increasing attention as a fast and low-cost approach for time-series prediction. Photonic reservoir computing utilizes the high speed, broad bandwidth, and spatial parallelism of light. However, the effect of the internal connection structure (network topology) on the computing performance has not been investigated for large-scale photonic reservoirs. In this study, we experimentally and numerically demonstrate photonic reservoir computing using a spatial light modulator to systematically evaluate the relationship between the network topology and the performance of reservoir computing. We introduce complex network structures such as small-world and scale-free network topologies of the internal nodes in the reservoir. We perform the memory capacity measurement and the one-step-ahead prediction task of the chaotic time series to compare the performance. We found that the small-world network exhibits the maximum memory capacity and the best prediction performance. Our numerical calculations reveal that the performance of the time-series prediction can be optimized by changing the rewiring probability of the network and the leak rate of the reservoir. We also implement photonic human brain network as a reservoir, which is designed by the connectomes of human brain activities. We found that the network topology strongly affects the performance of reservoir computing, and the small-world network structure outperforms the other configurations.
item.dc:creator: Sion Park, Kohei Watabe, Satoshi Sunada, Tomoki Yamagami, Atsushi Uchida

item.title: Approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser for reducing energy consumption
item.description: arXiv:2607.23288v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Photonic reservoir computing is a promising physical machine-learning approach for time-series prediction. Quantization of the reservoir response signal is an important consideration in the implementation of photonic reservoir computing, and the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency need to be optimized to achieve high prediction performance and low energy consumption. However, few studies have investigated the effects of the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency on both prediction performance and energy consumption. In this study, we introduce the concept of approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser by quantizing the reservoir node states and output weights. We numerically evaluate the performance of a chaotic time-series prediction task and estimate the energy consumption per sample using a component-level model. By optimizing the number of quantization bits, the sampling frequency, and the injection current of the semiconductor laser, we achieve a significant reduction in the estimated energy consumption per sample while maintaining prediction performance. We also obtain model-based estimates of the throughput, energy efficiency, and energy per operation of the proposed reservoir-computing system.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuki Ito, Kazutaka Kanno, Satoshi Kawakami, Atsushi Uchida

item.title: Breathing chimera states from purely triadic interactions
item.description: arXiv:2607.28017v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Chimera states, characterized by the coexistence of synchronized and desynchronized dynamics in identical oscillators, are typically studied in systems with pairwise interactions. Recent studies have shown that purely higher-order interactions can support chimera states. Here, we show that breathing chimera states arise in a model governed solely by a triadic phase interaction, whose intrinsic $\pi$-symmetry permits bimodal phase distributions. We construct a bimodal Ott-Antonsen reduction that incorporates an asymmetry parameter via prescribed asymmetric initial conditions, thereby achieving an exact low-dimensional description of the macroscopic dynamics. This allows us to derive an analytic condition for the emergence of chimera states and identify a bifurcation to a breathing chimera regime characterized by persistent oscillations. Furthermore, the reduced dynamics can be expressed as a Riccati-type equation, providing a geometric interpretation of the chimera state as a closed periodic orbit in the complex plane. Our results establish purely triadic coupling as a minimal higher-order mechanism for chimera formation and provide a tractable framework for studying symmetry-broken collective dynamics in systems dominated by many-body interactions.
item.dc:creator: Sudo Yi, Gug Young Kim, Mi Jin Lee, S. -W. Son, B. Kahng
